article_title: Trust calibration and perceived developmental gains in university students' collaboration with generative AI: an exploratory sequential mixed methods study
citation: Fan Bu and Wei Li (2026). Trust calibration and perceived developmental gains in university students' collaboration with generative AI: an exploratory sequential mixed methods study. Front. Psychol. 17:1861072. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1861072
title: A 22-item self-report instrument measuring contextual support, trust calibration, collaborative regulation, and perceived transfer gains
description: A five-point Likert-scale self-report instrument developed from the qualitative phase rather than assembled solely from pre-existing scales. "The ﬁnal instrument contained 22 items: six measuring contextual support, ﬁve measuring trust calibration, six measuring collaborative regulation, and ﬁve measuring perceived transfer gains." Items were reviewed by educational psychology researchers and higher education instructors, pilot tested with 94 undergraduates, and administered to a formal sample of 642 valid responses for CFA and SEM.
requirements: Items were drafted to represent one construct and one primary idea, avoiding double-barreled statements, technical terminology, and overly general evaluations of GenAI
constraints: Perceived-transfer-gain items capture subjective perceptions of developmental change across tasks rather than objectively demonstrated competence
target_learning_goals: measuring contextual conditions, trust judgments, regulatory behavior, and perceived developmental outcomes in GenAI-supported learning
examples: The formal survey distributed 680 questionnaires, received 654 returns, and retained 642 valid responses after quality screening
key_sources: Fan Bu and Wei Li (2026). Trust calibration and perceived developmental gains in university students' collaboration with generative AI: an exploratory sequential mixed methods study. Front. Psychol. 17:1861072. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1861072

article_title: The Effects of Using Concept Cartoons in Astronomy Subjects on Critical Thinking Skills among Seventh Grade Student
citation: Filiz Demirci, Cengiz Özyürek. (2017). The Effects of Using Concept Cartoons in Astronomy Subjects on Critical Thinking Skills among Seventh Grade Student. International Electronic Journal of Elementary Education, 10(2). https://doi.org/10.26822/iejee.2017236119
title: 22 researcher-developed concept cartoons for the Solar System and Beyond unit
description: The researchers created concept cartoons using common cartoon characters and the Scratch program, based on the 'Solar System and Beyond' unit content. The article states care was taken to create the concept cartoons in a way that they would help to develop students' critical thinking skills, and that the researchers tried to create at least three speech balloons (characters), which included different ways of thinking with content, in order to facilitate a discussion environment in the classroom. Experts in science education and astronomy reviewed all cartoons before use.
requirements: Expert review of conceptual framework and scientific expressions in speech balloons before classroom use
At least three speech balloons presenting different ways of thinking to facilitate discussion
constraints: Developed specifically for the seventh grade 'Solar System and Beyond' unit content
target_learning_goals: critical thinking skills in astronomy topics
examples: Cartoons were projected on the board, characters and their views introduced, and students asked which character's thoughts they agreed with and why
key_sources: Filiz Demirci, Cengiz Özyürek. (2017). The Effects of Using Concept Cartoons in Astronomy Subjects on Critical Thinking Skills among Seventh Grade Student. International Electronic Journal of Elementary Education, 10(2). https://doi.org/10.26822/iejee.2017236119

article_title: Position paper of Brazilian Society of Head and Neck Surgery among competencies in Head and Neck Surgery teaching for general Surgery residents.
citation: Ferrari de Castro Mario Augusto; Dedivitis Rogério Aparecido; Mendes de Matos Fátima Cristina; Nakai Marianne Yumi; de Matos Leandro Luongo; Kulcsar Marco Aurélio Vamondes; Chone Carlos Takahiro; Kowalski Luiz Paulo; Ferreira da Silva Julia Fonseca; Kuroiwa Thiago Yuuki. (2026). Position paper of Brazilian Society of Head and Neck Surgery among competencies in Head and Neck Surgery teaching for general Surgery residents. Brazilian Journal of Otorhinolaryngology. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bjorl.2026.101875
title: A 22-competency framework for general surgery residents in head and neck surgery
description: The article establishes a final framework of 22 essential competencies for general surgery residents in head and neck surgery, spanning professionalism, communication, teamwork, clinical evaluation, and specific procedures. Competencies include the ability to "Perform tracheostomy and/or cricothyroidotomy in patients with acute airway obstruction" and to "Evaluate, investigate, and develop an action plan for patients with acute airway obstruction". The framework is intended to standardize surgical education and guide curriculum development.
requirements: General Surgery residents and trainees should be trained for topics and procedures frequently encountered in general clinical practice
constraints: The consensus addresses highly prevalent aspects within the specialty, with situations beyond primary and secondary care levels experienced during subspecialty professional training
target_learning_goals: Head and neck surgery competencies including airway management, diagnosis of prevalent conditions, and surgical procedures
